clue.text: Circus act with men involved in accident

indicators.note: involved can mean tangled or complicated, so the letters before it are tangled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, nine letters of the mix
taken as written, the other three letters of the mix

explanation.surface: A big-top turn featuring several performers ends in a mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' tangles the letters of CIRCUS ACT together with MEN; 'with' only joins the two lots of fodder and 'in' leads to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in the older sense of a chance happening or event, as in 'a victim of ...'.

clue.text: Lords' agreement in substance

definitions.meaning: in the House of Lords, the upper chamber of the UK Parliament, a vote in favour is called this, where the Commons says aye
the matter or material held within something, such as the argument of a book

explanation.surface: The peers have agreed on the main points of a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: a peer's vote of assent in Parliament, and the matter something holds.

clue.text: Wandered through parts of Dover

indicators.note: the parts of the town's name are its letters, and wandering through them sends them straying into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the five letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone strolled around bits of a Kent port.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: 'Wandered through parts of' strays the letters of DOVER into a new order. Dover is the English Channel ferry port.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to have rambled or strayed about a place is exactly this past tense.

clue.text: Not reported for being without a hat

definitions.meaning: a news story that no journalist was sent to write up
bare-headed, as a man is when he removes his headgear

explanation.surface: Someone escaped a mention for going bare-headed.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: a story the press ignored, and a bare head.

clue.text: Try strikers for uprising

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising sends the word climbing, so it is read from the bottom up

parts.note: bats are things that strike a ball

explanation.surface: Workers who walked out are put on trial for a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns BATS upside down in this down entry; 'for' is only a link. The definition is the noun: to have a try at something is to have a go.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a noun: an attempt or go at something.

clue.text: Continental girl gets under skin of a man, perhaps

indicators.note: getting under a skin means going inside it, so the name goes within the outer letters
the skin is the outside layer, so only the first and last letters of the word are used

parts.note: Erica is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A European woman irritates a chap, possibly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skin of' takes the first and last letters of MAN, and 'gets under' puts ERICA inside them, after the clue's own A. 'perhaps' admits that the definition is only one example of someone from a continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: someone from the New World belongs to a continent just as a European does.

clue.text: Eccentric crook

definitions.meaning: an odd person with strange fixed ideas
a bend or bent arm, like the handle used to turn an engine

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: an oddball, and a bent arm or elbow-shaped handle.

clue.text: How the pedlar, say, gets about under pressure

definitions.text: How the pedlar, say, gets about under pressure

parts.words: How the pedlar, say, gets about under pressure
parts.note: pedlar said out loud is pedaller, someone who travels by pressing on pedals; pressure also hints at shoving, the first half of the British word for a bicycle

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman does his rounds while stressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you to hear pedlar as pedaller, and the pressure is what feet apply to pedals. The answer is a British word for an ordinary bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: a pedaller travels on a bicycle, driven by force from the feet.

clue.text: College boy

definitions.meaning: one of the colleges of Cambridge University, founded in 1882
a male first name, as borne by the politician Mr Lloyd and the actor Mr Froggitt

explanation.definitionFit: Two uses of one name: a Cambridge institution and a male forename.

clue.text: Probationary period for a service life?

definitions.text: Probationary period for a service life?

parts.words: Probationary period for a service life?
parts.note: service here is religious, not military: the trial time a newcomer spends before taking vows in a convent or monastery

explanation.surface: A recruit's trial months before a career in the forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service life' suggests the army or navy, but the service is divine: this is the trial time before entering a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: a newcomer to a monastery or convent serves this trial time before vows.

clue.text: A pleasing accent

parts.note: cute means attractive or charming

explanation.surface: Someone has a charming way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: The accent is not a way of speaking but a written mark, the one over the e in café.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: one of the marks written over a vowel, sloping up to the right.

clue.text: Left-over I have used in salads

definitions.note: an adjective phrase standing for the noun it describes, a leaf that goes into salads

parts.note: an end is a remnant, like a candle end or the end of a loaf
I have shortens to I've

explanation.surface: Yesterday's remains get tossed into the salad bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a description of the thing, not a noun for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a bitter leaf vegetable, related to chicory, eaten raw.

clue.text: After sprain, writer needs transport

indicators.note: the writer's name comes after the word for sprain, so the sprain goes first

parts.note: to rick your neck or back is to sprain or wrench it
George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright

explanation.surface: An author with a twisted ankle needs a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' fixes the order, the writer following the sprain; 'needs' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a light two-wheeled passenger vehicle pulled by a person.

clue.text: Bird out of the bible is name for an inn

indicators.note: out of here means outside of, so the bird stands round the bible

parts.note: a tern is a sea bird
AV is the Authorised Version, the King James Bible of 1611

explanation.surface: A pub is called after a bird mentioned in scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' seems to say a bird is taken from scripture; read it as 'outside of', a container. AV, the Authorised Version, is the 1611 King James Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an old word for a pub or public house.

clue.text: Girl on voyage calling at Mexican port

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it, so the girl's name comes first

parts.note: Vera is a girl's name

indicators.note: calling is speaking out loud, so the word for a voyage is heard and not spelt

parts.note: a cruise is a sea voyage for pleasure

explanation.surface: A young woman on a sea trip stops off in Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calling' makes CRUISE heard as CRUZ, and 'on' sets VERA above it in this down entry; 'at' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a city and harbour on the Gulf coast of that country.

clue.text: Boy about to imitate sort of camel

indicators.note: about means around, so the boy's name goes round the other word

parts.note: Brian is a boy's name
to act a part is to imitate or play someone

explanation.surface: A lad is on the point of doing an impression of a camel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'on the point of', but the two words split: 'about' alone is the container signal and 'to imitate' is a verb to be replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the two-humped kind from central Asia.

clue.text: Visit, carrying luggage, a distant connection

indicators.note: in a down clue the word below carries the one above it, so the visit sits under the luggage

parts.note: a trunk is a large travelling chest
to call on someone is to visit them

explanation.surface: Arriving with suitcases to stay with a remote relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts CALL beneath TRUNK in this down entry. The answer is the old British term for a long-distance telephone call, so the connection is a phone line, not a relative.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: a long-distance telephone link between two far-off exchanges.

clue.text: Loose kind of shirt tucked in will never fade

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the adjective that describes something everlasting

indicators.note: something tucked in is pushed inside, so the shirt letter goes within the other word

parts.note: loose morals are immoral ones
a T-shirt is named after its letter shape

explanation.surface: A baggy shirt worn inside the trousers keeps its colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked in' puts T inside IMMORAL. 'Loose' looks like the cut of the shirt but means lax in morals.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: something undying or everlasting lasts for all time.

clue.text: Explosive mixture ignited by power unit

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces stand side by side

parts.note: to fire something is to set it alight
the amp is a unit of electricity, strictly of current

explanation.surface: A volatile blend is set off by a generator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' sets the two pieces side by side. The answer is the miners' name for methane mixed with air in a coal pit.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: methane and air in a coal mine, which blows up when lit.

clue.text: Thin paper is unconvincing

definitions.meaning: a sheet of very light paper, once used for carbon copies in offices and newsrooms
weak and easily seen through, said of an excuse or argument

explanation.surface: A lightweight essay fails to persuade.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: a light sheet for carbon copies, and a weak excuse.

clue.text: It sounds as if old religious officials were bores

indicators.note: the phrase tells you the officials' name is heard, not spelt, giving a word said the same way

parts.note: augurs were priests of ancient Rome who read omens from the flight of birds

explanation.surface: By all accounts the priests of long ago were tedious company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It sounds as if' has AUGURS heard as a word spelt with an E. The bores are not dull people but tools that bore holes in wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: carpenters' tools that drill holes.

clue.text: Endlessly spray a plant

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the word for spray loses its last letter

parts.note: to syringe plants is to spray them with water from a garden syringe

explanation.surface: A gardener keeps misting a shrub without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' takes the final E off SYRINGE, and the clue's A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the botanical name of the lilac, also used for the mock orange.

clue.text: Hesitancy of the French lost 22

indicators.note: lost means gone missing, so the French word drops out of the longer one

parts.note: indecision is wavering, an inability to make up one's mind
de is French for of

explanation.surface: Dithering by French troops cost them twenty-two men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' drops DE from INDECISION. The number is not a quantity: it points to the answer at 22 down, a word for a cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym of the other entry: both are words for a cut, this one a surgeon's.

clue.text: Money kept in cummerbund in slit

indicators.note: something kept in a thing is held inside it, so the money letter goes within the garment

parts.note: a cummerbund is a broad sash worn round the waist with evening dress
L is the old abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Cash is hidden in an opening in a dinner-jacket waistband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept in' puts L inside SASH; the second 'in' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a long narrow cut, as in a garment.

clue.text: Broadcaster about the king is more biased

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word goes round the letter for the king

parts.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it by hand, the work of a sower; the setter spells that sower with an E
K is the abbreviation for king in chess and cards

explanation.surface: A television channel covering the monarch is less impartial than the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SEWER round K. The broadcaster scatters seed, properly a sower, so the spelling is the setter's liberty. The definition is whimsical: skew with -er added, as if a comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical comparative: something slanted to a greater degree, said of a spit for meat.

clue.text: Horse killed jumping in race

indicators.note: jumping is going upwards, so in a down clue the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: slew is the past tense of slay
H is the abbreviation for horse, also slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A steeplechaser dies at a fence during a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumping' turns SLEW upside down in this down entry, with H after it; 'in' is a link. The race is a people, not a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a people or nation, that of Cardiff and Snowdonia.

clue.text: Urge to jog

definitions.meaning: to push someone into action, to goad them
to nudge or poke, as one jogs an elbow or a memory

explanation.surface: A sudden desire to go for a run.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one verb: to goad into action and to nudge.

clue.text: Very little money in France, a bandmaster found

parts.note: sous were old French coins of tiny value, still the French word for small change

explanation.surface: A conductor is discovered in France with hardly a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' only tells you the answer has been reached. John Philip Sousa was the American composer of marches such as The Stars and Stripes Forever.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the American march king who led the US Marine Band.

clue.text: Sailor's girl's abbreviated sou-wester

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

indicators.note: abbreviated means cut short, so the girl's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Pauline is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A seaman's girlfriend has a cut-down waterproof hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abbreviated' takes the final E off PAULINE. A sou'wester is a sailor's waterproof hat, and the answer was once the name for a sailor's tarred hat too.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an old name for a seaman's waterproofed hat, as well as the canvas sheet.

clue.text: Curious phial out of a Greek temple site exhibited in US city

indicators.note: out of here means outside of, so the rearranged word stands round the other pieces
curious means odd or strange, so the next word's letters are put in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written, the five letters to rearrange
Delphi was the site of the temple of Apollo and its oracle

explanation.surface: A strange little bottle from an ancient shrine goes on show in an American museum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curious' makes PHILA, and 'out of' means outside of, not taken from, so those five letters split to stand round the rest; 'exhibited in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the largest town in Pennsylvania.
